title: Using predictive multiplicity to measure individual performance within the AI Act
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not conduct a benchmark related to faith or religion. It proposes a technical framework and metrics (conflict ratio, δ-ambiguity) to measure 'predictive multiplicity' and assess individual performance fairness in high-risk AI systems, in the context of the EU AI Act.
findings: This paper does not contain any findings related to religion or faith. Its analysis focuses on the technical and legal implications of 'predictive multiplicity'—where multiple models with similar overall accuracy can produce different outcomes for the same individual—and its relevance to the accuracy provisions of the EU AI Act.
